title: Approval, Booking Request and Appointment
description: The write path (§2.5, §7, §9). Carries the two hardest invariants in the project: no booking without a valid bound approval, and no double booking on retry.

state_version.description: The workflow version the patient approved against.

payload_hash.description: Hash of the exact booking payload the patient saw. Any data change — slot, provider, visit type, preferences — invalidates the approval, because the hash no longer matches (§9).

expires_at.description: Approval is time-bounded. An expired approval is never extended implicitly — the patient is asked again.

granted_by.title: ApprovalGrantedBy
granted_by.description: The final booking always requires patient approval, even after human intervention (§7, §11): an operator's resolution returns to a safe state, it does not grant booking consent.

consumed.description: Set when a booking write takes it. A consumed approval cannot authorise a second write — this is a structural guard against double booking, not just a validation rule.

invalidated_reason.title: ApprovalInvalidationReason
invalidated_reason.description: Optional: absent means the approval is still valid.

BookingPayload.$comment: This object is the hashed unit. Two payloads that differ in any field must produce different hashes, so an approval can never be replayed against a changed booking.

idempotency_key.description: Sent to the hospital adapter. On outcome_unknown the SAME key is re-used for lookup and reconcile — a second, independent key is never minted (§7).

external_reference.description: The hospital-side identifier once it exists. Null while REQUESTED or unresolved.

reschedule_of.description: Set when this request replaces an earlier booking. §2.5: the old booking is cancelled only AFTER the new one is verified — never before.

status.title: ReconciliationStatus
status.description: Driven by lookup_request against the same idempotency key until it resolves or escalates (§7).

ReconciliationState.$comment: While status is `pending` the booking is shown as UNVERIFIED, never as confirmed and never as failed (§2.5: HTTP 200 is not a confirmation, and an unknown outcome is not a rejection).

idempotency_key.description: Every attempt for one logical booking carries the SAME key. A differing key on a retry is the double-booking bug this field exists to catch.

result.title: BookingAttemptResult
result.description: `timeout_before_commit` and `timeout_after_commit` are distinct outcomes (§17) and lead to different next steps: only the latter creates a booking that must be reconciled.

raw_response_ref.description: Pointer to the stored vendor payload. Kept for the adapter-normalisation evidence, never shown to the patient.

verified.description: True only after the appointment was read back from the hospital. A receipt is never rendered from a local optimistic write.

verification_method.title: AppointmentVerificationMethod
verification_method.description: Optional: absent means the appointment has not been verified yet.

AppointmentRecord.$comment: REQUESTED and PENDING_REVIEW must never be rendered as a confirmed appointment (§2.5). The receipt component branches on `state` AND `verified`, not on HTTP status.

status.title: OutboxStatus
status.description: Written in the SAME transaction as the booking (§7). A notification failure never rolls the booking back, and a permanently failed notification stops rather than looping forever (§16).
